content:
marie: Heads-up — ACME reported streaming metrics in Console showing TTFT and tokens/sec dipping into negative values between ~09:08-09:14 UTC for a handful of routes. Customer says app-facing latency didn’t spike, it's purely dashboard/analytics. attaching quick screenshot in thread :point_down:

alex: Can you paste the raw query we use to build that dashboard? Also which model/route?

marie: Route: /v1/stream/gen (tenant acme-prod). Quick rollup query from ClickHouse (last 24h window around the incident):
```
SELECT time_bucket, sum(tokens) as tokens_sum, sum(ttft_ms) as ttft_sum, count(*)
FROM streaming_rollups
WHERE tenant = 'acme-prod' AND time >= '2026-03-15 08:50' AND time <= '2026-03-15 09:20'
GROUP BY time_bucket ORDER BY time_bucket
```
Result snippet: time_bucket=09:08 tokens_sum=125000, 09:09 tokens_sum=-42000, 09:10 tokens_sum=130000, 09:11 tokens_sum=-5000

jonas: Negative sums usually mean the rollup delta was applied with an inverted delta or there was an out-of-order write with negative signed delta. Any consumer restarts or replays on the metric topic around 09:10?

priya: SRE telemetry — noticed the streaming-metrics consumer (consumer group: rollup-aggregator) restarted at 2026-03-15T09:11:57Z on node infra-09, because of OOM kill. Offsets jumped back by ~1200 messages and then continued. Log excerpt:
```
[sre-bot] 2026-03-15T09:11:57Z consumer rollup-aggregator crashed: OOMKilled
[sre-bot] 2026-03-15T09:12:04Z consumer rollup-aggregator restarted, resumed at offset 3289002
[sre-bot] 2026-03-15T09:12:08Z processed message with timestamp 2026-03-15T09:08:42Z (out-of-order)
```

kevin: That matches a hypothesis: the aggregator computes deltas per partition and emits +/− deltas; if a replayed segment is applied it can subtract earlier totals producing negative 'tokens' sums in the time bucket. We saw something similar last year when prefix caching caused duplicate upstream emits.

alex: Repro checklist for eng-runtime: 1) Find the offending messages in Kafka topic streaming-metrics-v1 (offset window ~3287600-3289000). 2) Re-run aggregator locally with those messages to see if deltas flip sign. 3) Check whether rollup uses 32-bit int anywhere.

jonas: Quick local repro I ran: pulled the batch and replayed it into the aggregator with original timestamps preserved. Output: one time_bucket had tokens_delta = -42000 due to a duplicate negative delta record from the delta normalizer. Patch idea: clamp deltas to >= -existing_count and use int64 for aggregates.

marie: Customer update: told them we’re investigating, asked for tolerance window, they said they’re mostly worried about billing graphs (they use tokens/sec in invoices). Need a mitigation ASAP.

priya: Mitigation options: A) Temporarily hide rollup-based tokens/sec on Console for affected tenant/time ranges (fast, UI toggle). B) Disable delta normalization step in aggregator and fall back to raw counters for 30m backfill. C) Backfill corrected rollups by replay + dedupe job.

kevin: For minimal customer impact, propose path B then C: 1) Disable delta normalizer (feature-flag) for streaming-aggregator for 10 mins to stop further negative writes. 2) Queue a backfill job that computes absolute counts by scanning raw events (idempotent) and re-writes the rollup buckets. 3) Add a clamp in aggregator code for safety.

alex: I’ll own the code change for clamp + int64. jonas, can you handle the rollback/feature-flag? priya, can SRE run the temporary flag and confirm consumer stability?

jonas: Yep. Feature-flag flip command (run from infra-admin pod):
```
curl -XPOST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \
  https://admin.redwood-inference/internal/flags/streaming-aggregator/disable-delta-normalizer
```
I’ll also patch helm chart to restart aggregator with increased memory for infra-09: set resources.requests.memory to "6Gi".

priya: On it — scaling infra-09 up + flip flag now. Will monitor for consumer restarts.

sre-bot: [automated] flag disable-delta-normalizer set at 2026-03-15T09:18:03Z by priya. Aggregator pods rolling restart initiated.

marie: Customer notified about temporary dashboard change; they asked for ETA on backfill.

alex: ETA: patch + canary deploy ~ 2h. Backfill job depending on scan size ~ 45m to 2h. I'll open a PR and link it here.

marie: Thanks all. Action items: alex PR + deploy, jonas helm bump + flag ops, priya monitor + confirm no further negative deltas, kevin schedule backfill. Will follow up to ensure billing graphs corrected.

kevin: Also created ticket INFRA-2147 to add defensive tests and alerts for negative rollup sums (threshold alert when tokens_sum < 0).

marie: marking this thread as the escalation. If anyone sees additional tenants affected, ping here. :white_check_mark:
